facts.statement: Sabinosuchus is a genus of mesoeucrocodylian from the Maastrichtian Escondido Formation in Coahuila, Mexico, with Sabinosuchus coahuilensis as its type species.
facts.quote: Sabinosuchus (meaning "Sabinas crocodile") is a genus of mesoeucrocodylian from the Maastrichtian Escondido Formation of Coahuila, Mexico, with Sabinosuchus coahuilensis as the type species.

facts.statement: Sabinosuchus was first described as a dyrosaurid in 2016 but was later reclassified as a pholidosaurid in 2020.
facts.quote: First described as a putative dyrosaurid by Shiller II et al. (2016), it was later recovered as a pholidosaurid by Jouve & Jalil (2020).

facts.statement: Amateur paleontologists from the group Palaeontologos Aficionados de Sabinas A.C. discovered Sabinosuchus in Mexico in 2002.
facts.quote: Sabinosuchus was discovered by amateur paleontologist of the Palaeontologos Aficionados de Sabinas A.C. (PASAC) in 2002 in Mexico.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Sabinosuchus come from the Maastrichtian Escondido Formation, though earlier reports incorrectly attributed them to the Olmos Formation.
facts.quote: All fossils of Sabinosuchus found by the team stem from the Maastrichtian Escondido Formation, although earlier reports wrongfully believed them to stem from the underlying Olmos Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype material was catalogued as specimens PAS 945 to PAS 949 and PAS 952 after being reassembled into an almost complete specimen.
facts.quote: The holotype material was initially catalogued as specimens PAS 945 to PAS 949 and PAS 952 once reassembled to form an almost complete specimen.

facts.statement: A second specimen, catalogued as PAS 950 and PAS 951, consists of a rostrum fragment and an articulated mandible piece.
facts.quote: The other specimen, catalogued as PAS 950 and PAS 951, represents a part of the rostrum alongside an articulated piece of the mandible.

facts.statement: All Sabinosuchus specimens were donated to the El Museo Muzquiz.
facts.quote: All specimens were donated to the El Museo Muzquiz.

facts.statement: The name Sabinosuchus combines the town of Sabinas near the discovery site with the Greek word Souchos for crocodile.
facts.quote: The name Sabinosuchus is a combination of Sabinas, a town near the type locality, and the Greek Souchos (crocodile).

facts.statement: The species name coahuilensis refers to the state of Coahuila where the specimen was found.
facts.quote: The species name is likewise based on the area the specimen was found, referring to the state of Coahuila.

facts.statement: Sabinosuchus was a longirostrine animal with a proportionally long and slender snout.
facts.quote: Sabinosuchus was a longirostrine animal, meaning its snout was proportionally long and slender.

facts.statement: The nasal bones of Sabinosuchus are unfused and covered in teardrop-shaped pits, making them the most ornamented skull bone.
facts.quote: The nasal bones are unfused over their preserved length and covered in teardrop-shaped pits making it the most ornamented skull bone.

facts.statement: The mandible of Sabinosuchus is approximately 92 cm long, with less than half consisting of the mandibular symphysis.
facts.quote: The mandible is approximately 92 cm long, less than half of that consisting of the mandibular symphysis.

facts.statement: The better preserved dentary contained nineteen alveoli, totaling twenty-one alveoli after a 2020 re-examination.
facts.quote: The better preserved of the two dentaries preserved nineteen alveoli, adding up to a total of twenty-one following the 2020 examination.

facts.statement: Most dentary alveoli in Sabinosuchus are circular and range in diameter from 2.2 to 4.4 cm.
facts.quote: Most dentary alveoli are circular in shape and range in diameter from 2.2-4.4 cm.

facts.statement: Sabinosuchus teeth were generally robust with slight curvature toward the snout tip, but showed more developed curvature and compression in the rear jaw from the seventeenth tooth onward.
facts.quote: The teeth are generally robust with a slight curvature towards the tip of the snout, but with better developed curviture and slight anteroposterior compression in the rear portions of the jaw (at least from the seventeenth dentary tooth onward).

facts.statement: Sabinosuchus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sabinosuchus belongs to the parent group Pholidosauridae.
Sabinosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
The original assignment of Sabinosuchus to Dyrosauridae was poorly supported according to its describers.
facts.quote: Overall, while first described as a putative dyrosaur, Schiller and colleagues make note that this assignment was poorly supported.
